خُشَارٌ (K) and ↓ خُشَارَةٌ (S, A, K) The bad part or parts [or the refuse] (Lh, S, K) of goods, or commodities, (Lh,) or of anything. (S, K.) And the latter, The worst kind, syn. شِيص, of lates. (A.) ―
-b2- What contains no لُبّ [or heart], of barley. (A, K.) ―
-b3- And the latter, The refuse of food remaining upon a table; that in which is no good. (S, A, K. *) ―
-b4- Also the latter, (S, A, K,) and the former, (K,) and ↓ خُشَّارٌ , (IAar,) (tropical:) The refuse, or lowest or basest or meanest sort, of mankind, or of people; (IAar, S, A, K;) as also ↓ خَاشِرٌ , accord. to the K, but correctly ↓ خَاشِرَةٌ , as related by AA from IAar. (TA.) El-Hotei-ah says, “وَبَاعَ بَنِيهِ بَعْضُهُمْ بِخُشَارَةً
وَبِعْتَ لِذُبْيَانَ العَلَآءَ بِمَالِكِ
” [And some of them have sold their sons for the refuse of mankind; but] thou hast purchased eminence for Dhubyán with Málik: in the S we find بِمَالِكَا [with thy property]: but it is correctly as above: Málik was a son of 'Oyeyneh Ibn- Hisn: the Benoo-'Ámir slew him: wherefore 'Oyeyneh made war upon them, and obtained his blood-revenge, and spoil: and to this event El- Hotei-ah refers in the verse above. (IB, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
